title: The Arched Residence
seo_description: A residential interior concept in Lahore layering arched openings, exposed timber and woven textures into a calm, grounded home.

gallery.alt: Arched interior with woven seating and warm timber
Sunlit living area with natural textures
Warm kitchen and living junction with timber joinery

body:
The thinking behind the space

A home that feels like a deep breath. This residential concept explores a softer way of living, with generous daylight, tactile finishes, and a warm, grounded palette.

The approach

The room begins with its architecture. Arched openings frame the garden, while exposed timber creates a quiet rhythm overhead. Low, comfortable seating keeps sightlines open and lets the proportions of the space do the talking.

The finer details

A mix of woven textures and soft upholstery gives the scheme its depth. Rather than relying on decoration, the palette draws character from the natural variation of wood, linen, and stone.

Sample concept, not a completed client commission. Gallery images illustrate the design direction and may depict different properties.

title: The Open House
seo_description: An open-plan family home concept with timber screens, a sculptural staircase and a clear separation of busy and quiet zones.

gallery.alt: Open dining area with timber screens and a sculptural staircase
Dining setting with warm timber and soft lighting

body:
A plan that breathes

Open planning only works when the quiet moments survive. Here, a central stair anchors the plan, while timber screens soften the line between cooking, eating and gathering.

Zones without walls

Furniture and light do the dividing. A long bench follows the window wall, and a deep rug marks the living zone without closing it off from the garden.

title: The Collective Workspace
seo_description: A workplace interior concept built around focus rooms, warm timber and a shared table that brings a hybrid team together.

gallery.alt: Workspace corridor with glass partitions and timber detail
Communal meeting area with wooden tables and large windows

body:
Work that people want to return to

A hybrid team needs a reason to come in. This concept puts a generous shared table at the centre of the plan, with quieter focus rooms tucked behind glass.

Warmth at work

Timber baffles soften acoustics and sightlines, while felt panels and planting absorb the harder edges of a working day.

title: The Oak Edit
seo_description: A bespoke joinery concept in solid oak: a kitchen island, wardrobe wall and reading bench designed as one family of pieces.

gallery.alt: Oak kitchen island with integrated seating
Bedroom with full-height timber wardrobe wall

body:
One family of pieces

The most convincing interiors are made of parts that understand each other. This concept treats the kitchen island, wardrobe wall and reading bench as one family, sharing a 45-degree detail and a single oak specification.

Made to be used

Surfaces are sealed for daily life, edges are eased by hand, and hardware is chosen to disappear.

title: The Soft Retreat
seo_description: A bedroom concept in muted green, linen and woven lighting, designed for rest with layered light and quiet storage.

gallery.alt: Bedroom with muted green bedding and woven pendant
Calm bedroom with timber furniture and soft textiles

body:
Rest as the brief

This concept starts with light: three layers, none of them overhead-bright. A woven pendant, wall sconces and a low lamp do the work after dark.

Softness with structure

Rounded furniture sits against a crisp architectural frame, and the storage disappears into the wall so the room can stay uncluttered.

title: The Gathering Room
seo_description: A hospitality-led meeting room concept with a long communal table, natural light and acoustic timber ceilings.

gallery.alt: Communal meeting room with long timber table and large windows
Long dining table set for a gathering

body:
Room to gather

One long table, daylight on two sides, and enough space behind every chair to have a private word. The concept borrows more from hospitality than from the office.

Acoustics as comfort

Timber slats and clay plaster keep the room warm in tone and calm in sound.
